subject: Temporary uptime waiver & rolling credit pool proposal
messages:
From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@streamline.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <p.shah@streamline.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streamline: SLA redlines + temporary migration window ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — we appreciate how predictable Redwood’s hosted API looks. We ran your SLA draft past our ops and procurement folks and have a couple of asks before we proceed with the pilot. I attached the redlined SLA (Streamline-SLA-draft-2027-08-24.pdf).

Two main items:
- Migration window waiver: We have a planned data/traffic migration during Sept that will create predictable short windows of degraded availability (spikes and brief queueing). We’d like a 60‑day temporary waiver from the standard uptime credit triggers for those expected windows.
- Rolling credit pool: rather than monthly line‑item credits, we’d prefer a rolling credit pool that accumulates across months during ramp so we don’t keep opening PR cases for small dips. Our ask is the pool be limited to 12% of the monthly committed spend during the pilot.

A few clarifying questions embedded in the redline (see page 4): how do you treat planned maintenance (notify window + excluded minutes), and how do latency SLO misses map to availability credits?

Happy to hop on a quick call to run through.

Thanks,
Aaron
Aaron Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, Streamline AI
Attachments: Streamline-SLA-draft-2027-08-24.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline: SLA redlines + temporary migration window ask

Aaron — appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Looping in Marissa (AE) and Karthik (SLA/product) to help with a concise counterproposal. Quick thoughts before we sync:

- Standard baseline: Redwood’s hosted SLA for production customers is 99.95% availability measured monthly. Credits are tiered and prorated against the invoice for the affected month.
- Migration waiver: we can offer a temporary exception for predictable migration work, but we need defined windows and pre-notification (at least 7 days). We typically permit a 30–90 day waiver for migrations with clear windows; given your ask we can agree to a 60‑day waiver if the migration schedule is confirmed and the total waived minutes are bounded.
- Rolling credit pool: we like the idea of consolidating small dips. Our internal concern is runaway liability; we can support a pooled credit up to a negotiated cap during ramp.

Proposed counter (high level):
1) Baseline stays 99.95% monthly availability outside exemption windows.
2) Migration exemption: 60‑day window starting on the date you confirm; during that window credit triggers for availability below 99.95% will not apply for pre-registered maintenance blocks (each block must be logged in advance). Any unplanned outages during the window remain eligible for credits.
3) Rolling credit pool for pilot: credits will be accrued into a pool and applied against invoices over a 6‑month ramp period. We propose a cap of 10% of monthly committed spend (not 12%), with credits applied to invoices monthly until the pool is exhausted or expires at the end of the ramp.

Karthik — can you confirm how latency SLOs would map to credit triggers (we typically charge latency as a separate remediation only when p95 exceeds the agreed threshold for >72 consecutive hours).

Aaron — can you send the proposed migration schedule (start/end + anticipated maintenance blocks) and we’ll draft exact language for legal and Marissa will update pricing language. If agreeable we can have an internal term sheet by Friday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@streamline.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <p.shah@streamline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 08:57:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline: SLA redlines + temporary migration window ask

Thanks Tessa — that helps. Couple follow-ups inline:

> "Migration exemption: 60‑day window starting on the date you confirm; during that window credit triggers for availability below 99.95% will not apply for pre-registered maintenance blocks"

Agreed in principle. Two asks: 1) allow us up to four pre-registered maintenance blocks (each up to 8 hours) within the 60 days without triggering credits, and 2) allow a single emergency rollback block (we’ll notify within 24 hours post-facto).

> "Rolling credit pool for pilot: cap of 10% of monthly committed spend"

We’re comfortable moving from 12% down to 10% only if the pool can carry over across months without expiring for at least 90 days, and if there’s a mechanism to convert unused pool credits into a one-time invoice credit at pilot end.

Also — can you clarify whether scheduled maintenance (Redwood-initiated) during business hours falls under the exemption or if that still counts toward availability? That’s particularly important as our traffic is spiky and business hours outages are costly for us.

I attached a short traffic snapshot (streamline-traffic-snapshot-aug.csv) so you can see the ramp patterns.

If we can get firm answers on the four-block allowance, emergency rollback, 90‑day carryover, and scheduled maintenance treatment, we can move to a legal review.

—Aaron

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lee <aaron.lee@streamline.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streamline: SLA redlines + temporary migration window ask

Aaron — thanks for the detailed feedback and the traffic snapshot. Quick confirmation and final counter to keep procurement moving:

1) Pre-registered blocks: we can accept up to four pre-registered maintenance blocks (max 8 hours each) during the 60‑day migration window. Those blocks will be excluded from credit triggers provided they are logged at least 7 days in advance. The emergency rollback block (one per migration) is allowed; Redwood requires a post‑event notification within 24 hours.

2) Rolling credit pool mechanics (final):
   - Pool accrues credited amount from any month during pilot where availability falls below 99.95% (outside pre-registered blocks).
   - Pool cap: 10% of monthly committed spend (applies per month while the pilot is active).
   - Carryover: unused pool credits roll forward for 90 days. Any remaining pool balance at pilot end may be applied as a one-time invoice credit within 30 days post‑pilot (subject to standard accounting reconciliation).

3) Scheduled maintenance triggered by Redwood: planned maintenance initiated by Redwood that has been announced with >= 72 hours notice and falls within Redwood’s published maintenance windows will be excluded from availability calculations. Unsigned/unannounced maintenance or emergency maintenance that materially impacts you will be handled case-by-case and may be eligible for credits.

4) Latency SLOs: our latency remediation is separate from availability. For this pilot we will keep the existing latency SLO at p95 < 300ms. Latency-based credits will trigger only for sustained p95 breaches longer than 72 consecutive hours and will be calculated separately — they do not get added to the availability pool but can be converted to invoice credits by mutual agreement.

Next steps: Marissa will update the commercial term sheet to reflect the 60‑day migration window with up to 4 pre‑registered blocks, the rolling credit pool capped at 10% with 90‑day carryover, and the maintenance carveouts described. Legal drafts will follow and we’ll share a DocuSign link once both sides sign the term sheet.

If that aligns with Streamline we’ll target a legal review early next week.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product & Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachments: (none)
